title: IELTS estimated-band assessment output
description: The only shape a scoring model may return. Free text outside this object is not accepted. Applies to writing (4 criteria) and speaking (3 criteria).

status.description: scored = a band was produced from the response. insufficient = the response cannot be scored; no band may be invented.

estimated.description: Always true. The product reports an estimated band, never an official IELTS result.

overall_band.description: Mean of the criterion bands, rounded to the nearest half band (.25 and .75 round up). null when status is insufficient.

criteria.description: Exactly 4 items for writing, exactly 3 for speaking. Empty when status is insufficient.

why.description: At most 2 sentences. Must describe what this candidate actually did, and must refer to the text in `quote`. Generic band-descriptor wording is not accepted.

quote.description: A verbatim span copied from the candidate's own response/transcript, 3-25 words. Never invented, never taken from the task prompt.

lowest_criterion.description: The `name` of the weakest criterion; on a tie, the one that costs the candidate most. null when status is insufficient.

rewrites.description: At most 3. Each takes one of the candidate's own sentences and shows a band-7 version of it. Empty when status is insufficient.

better.description: The same idea rewritten at band 7. Must keep the candidate's meaning; must not add new content.

what_changed.description: At most 1 sentence naming the change.

next_step.description: One concrete, actionable instruction, at most 1 sentence. Always present, including when status is insufficient.

insufficient_reason.description: Required when status is insufficient, absent otherwise.

word_count.description: Optional. Candidate words counted by the scorer (writing) or candidate words in the transcript (speaking).

criteria.name: task_response
criteria.why: The two rising lines are named but no percentages are taken from the chart, and nothing in the answer states the overall pattern.
criteria.quote: the recycling of Marden was going up and up every year

criteria.name: coherence_cohesion
criteria.why: The answer is one undivided block and sentence boundaries break down, so the reader has to work out where each comparison ends.
criteria.quote: in 2010 it is more, after that Hallowfield was down. and Trentbury

criteria.name: lexical_resource
criteria.why: Chart vocabulary is adequate but 'go up' and 'go down' carry almost every comparison in the answer.
criteria.quote: Trentbury go up slowly and Hallowfield go down slowly

criteria.name: grammatical_range_accuracy
criteria.why: Comparatives and past forms are attempted, but subject-verb agreement fails in most sentences and one clause has no main verb.
criteria.quote: The three towns was different from each other

rewrites.original: Trentbury go up slowly and Hallowfield go down slowly
rewrites.better: Trentbury rose steadily while Hallowfield declined at a similar pace.
rewrites.what_changed: Fixed subject-verb agreement and replaced the repeated 'go up / go down' with trend verbs.

examples.next_step: Add a short overview sentence that names the biggest rise and the biggest fall, each with a figure from the chart.
Write a full answer of at least 150 words that responds to the task before asking for an estimate.
